questions.stem:
Universal indicator contains several dyes. The reversible reaction of one dye, IndOH, is shown.

IndOH(aq) + H⁺(aq) ⇌ Ind⁺(aq) + H₂O(l)
colour X    colour Y

A few drops of Universal indicator solution are added to 50 cm³ of water.

A few drops of dilute hydrochloric acid are added to the solution.

Which row describes what happens when the acid is added?

options.label: A
options.text: pH decreases; colour of solution shifts towards colour X

options.label: B
options.text: pH decreases; colour of solution shifts towards colour Y

options.label: C
options.text: pH increases; colour of solution shifts towards colour X

options.label: D
options.text: pH increases; colour of solution shifts towards colour Y

figures.description: Options table with columns 'pH' and 'colour of solution shifts towards'. A: decreases, colour X. B: decreases, colour Y. C: increases, colour X. D: increases, colour Y.

questions.stem:

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: HNO₃(aq) has a lower formula mass than HCl(aq).

options.label: C
options.text: The HNO₃(aq) is more concentrated than the HCl(aq).

options.label: D
options.text: The HCl(aq) has dissociated more than the HNO₃(aq).

questions.stem:
Element X is in Group 1.

Some statements about element X are given.

- X is not the least dense element in Group 1.
- X is more reactive than potassium.
- X has an Aᵣ value less than 100.

Which element is X?

Three statements about the properties of metals are shown.

1 All metals conduct electricity.
2 All metals have two electrons in their innermost shell.
3 All metals have high melting points.

Which statements are correct?

Group 1 elements and transition elements are metals.

Student X suggests that the Group 1 elements are above hydrogen in the reactivity series but that not all transition elements are above hydrogen.

Student Y suggests that the densities of Group 1 elements are lower than those of the transition elements.

Which students are correct?

The equations for some of the reactions of metals Q, R and T are shown.

2QNO₃(aq) + Cu(s) → 2Q(s) + Cu(NO₃)₂(aq)
R(s) + TSO₄(aq) → T(s) + RSO₄(aq)
T(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → TSO₄(aq) + H₂(g)

Using the equations, what is the order of reactivity of Q, R and T?

options.label: B
options.text: most reactive R, Q, T least reactive

options.label: C
options.text: most reactive R, T, Q least reactive

options.text: most reactive T, R, Q least reactive

figures.description: Options table giving the order of reactivity from most reactive (left) to least reactive (right), with an arrow between the headings. A: Q, T, R. B: R, Q, T. C: R, T, Q. D: T, R, Q.

questions.stem:
Zinc is used to galvanise iron, which prevents the iron from rusting. Which statements are correct?

1 The layer of zinc forms a barrier between the iron and the oxygen and water in the atmosphere.
2 Zinc will oxidise before the iron does, even if the layer of zinc is scratched.
3 When iron rusts, atoms of iron gain electrons to form ions.

Some metals and the compounds in their ores are shown.

| metal | Al | Ca | Pb | Na | Fe | Mg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| compound in ore | Al₂O₃ | CaCO₃ | PbS | NaCl | Fe₂O₃ | MgCO₃ |

Which type of reaction occurs in the extraction of each of these metals from its ore?

figures.description: Two-row table. Metal: Al, Ca, Pb, Na, Fe, Mg. Compound in ore: Al₂O₃, CaCO₃, PbS, NaCl, Fe₂O₃, MgCO₃ respectively.

questions.stem:
Three statements about the carbon cycle are given.

1 The carbon cycle regulates the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
2 During photosynthesis, carbon dioxide is produced.
3 Combustion of hydrocarbons requires oxygen.

Which statements are correct?

CFC compounds were used as aerosol propellants. The structure of one CFC compound is shown.

Which element in this compound causes a depletion of ozone in the atmosphere?

questions.notes: Handwritten mark beside option A (not transcribed). Subscripts verified at 800 dpi: A C₃H₆, B C₃H₈.

questions.notes: Options verified at 600 dpi. As printed, A (11 C) and B (12 C) do not balance; C and D balance. The '?' at the end of the stem is very faint in the scan.

questions.stem:
Two statements are shown.

1 When ethanol is made from glucose by fermentation, each glucose molecule produces three molecules of ethanol.
2 When ethanoic acid is made from ethanol, the ethanol acts as an oxidising agent.

Which row about these statements is correct?

key
✓ = true
✗ = false

figures.description: Options table with columns 'statement 1' and 'statement 2', and a key at the right: ✓ = true, ✗ = false. Statement 1 column: A ✓, B ✓, C ✗, D ✗. The statement 2 column is empty in this scan (its ticks and crosses did not print), so options A/B and C/D look identical. The usual layout would be A ✓ ✓, B ✓ ✗, C ✗ ✓, D ✗ ✗, but that is not visible on the page.

questions.notes: The statement 2 column is printed blank (checked at 300 dpi; no faint marks), so A=B and C=D as printed. The usual pattern would be A ✓✓, B ✓✗, C ✗✓, D ✗✗ (the P1 key gives D), but that is inferred and not transcribed. Handwritten marks around the question number.
